title: Strategic alignment: Leveraging information technology for transforming organizations
supporting_sentence: PARAPHRASE: Strategic alignment is presented as the fit between business strategy and IT strategy, and as a continuing managerial process rather than a one-off design decision.
relevance: Foundational business-IT alignment model; frames the fit between organisational strategy and IT as a management problem.

title: The DeLone and McLean Model of Information Systems Success: A Ten-Year Update
supporting_sentence: PARAPHRASE: The ten-year update of the IS success model treats information quality, system quality and service quality as separate dimensions feeding use and net benefits.
relevance: Defines IS success as a multi-dimensional construct (quality, use, satisfaction, net benefit); anchors the claim that system quality and information quality are distinct.

title: Design Science in Information Systems Research1
authors: Hevner, A.R.; March, S.T.; Park, J.; Ram, S.
supporting_sentence: PARAPHRASE: Design science creates and evaluates artefacts intended to solve identified organisational problems, with relevance and rigour as twin requirements.
relevance: Canonical DSR framing: design artefacts are built and evaluated against organisational problems. Cited where the paper adopts DSR.

title: A Design Science Research Methodology for Information Systems Research
authors: Peffers, K.; Tuunanen, T.; Rothenberger, M.A.; Chatterjee, S.
supporting_sentence: PARAPHRASE: A design science research methodology is proposed comprising six steps from problem identification through demonstration and evaluation to communication.
relevance: Provides the DSR process model (problem identification, objectives, design, demonstration, evaluation, communication) used to structure this paper's evaluation.

title: Positioning and Presenting Design Science Research for Maximum Impact1
supporting_sentence: PARAPHRASE: Design science research should be positioned by the kind of knowledge it contributes, and its claims should be presented so that contribution type and evaluation are explicit.
relevance: Distinguishes design-science contributions by the type of knowledge claimed; supports the paper's explicit statement of what kind of contribution it makes.

title: Design and natural science research on information technology
supporting_sentence: PARAPHRASE: Research on IT spans design research, which builds artefacts, and natural-science research, which seeks to explain; the two have different truth criteria.
relevance: Separates design research from natural-science research; justifies reporting an artefact plus its evaluation rather than a hypothesis test alone.

title: A systematic literature review of pre-requirements specification traceability
authors: Mucha, J.; Kaufmann, A.; Riehle, D.
supporting_sentence: PARAPHRASE: A systematic literature review characterises pre-requirements specification traceability, its motivations and the difficulties reported in establishing it.
relevance: Systematic review of pre-requirements-specification traceability; supports the operational definition of traceability coverage and the claim that traceability is often incomplete in practice.

title: Rastreabilidade de Requisitos em Metodologias Ágeis: um Estudo Exploratório
venue: Anais do Simpósio Brasileiro de Sistemas de Informação (SBSI)
supporting_sentence: PARAPHRASE: An exploratory study examines how requirements traceability is practised in agile methodologies, reporting the difficulties teams encounter.
relevance: Brazilian (SBSI) exploratory study of requirements traceability in agile methods; satisfies the venue's SOL-coverage expectation with directly relevant work.

title: Investigando a Rastreabilidade de Requisitos em Ecossistemas de Software
authors: Gonçalves, R.; Malcher, P.; Santos, R.P.d.
venue: Anais Estendidos do XVIII Simpósio Brasileiro de Sistemas de Informação (SBSI Estendido 2022)
supporting_sentence: PARAPHRASE: Requirements traceability is investigated in the context of software ecosystems, where independently evolving systems complicate the tracing of requirements.
relevance: Brazilian (SBSI) work on requirements traceability in software ecosystems; second SOL source, showing traceability is an active concern in the national community.
